test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A train P travelling at a speed of 15 m/s is able to cross a platform of 200 meter length completely in 30 seconds. Approximately how long will it take train P to cross a man who is coming towards the train on his bike at a speed of 27 km/h? [Note: Ignore the length of the bike.]
solution:
**Given:**

Train P travelling at a speed of 15m/s covers 200m in 30 seconds.

Speed of a man on a bike = 27 km/h.

**Calculations:**

Let the length of the train = x.

Now, According to the question:

Distance = Speed × Time

(200 + x) = 15 × 30

⇒200 + x = 450

⇒x = 250 m

Hence, the length of the train is 250 m.

Now, the speed of a man on the bike is given 27 km/h

= 27 × (5)/(18) m/s

= 7.5 m/s

So, Time taken by train to pass the man is 

= Distance/ Speed (Here distance is the length of the train and speed = relative speed)

= (250)/(15+7.5)

= (250)/(22.5)

= 11.1 seconds

**Hence, The time taken by the train to pass the man is 11.1 seconds.**
